ai.description: *Eublepharis hardwickii* (Eublepharidae) reaches 20 cm. It features a yellow-banded, dark brown body with a white-tipped tail. Distinctive features include movable eyelids and a thick, bulbous tail.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eublepharis hardwickii* is uniquely identified by its distinct, broad white nuchal collar that extends across the nape, separating the head from the body pattern.
ai.habitat: *Eublepharis hardwickii* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in eastern India, typically found at low-to-moderate elevations in rocky, leaf-littered environments.
ai.behavior: The Eastern Indian Leopard Gecko is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to actively forage for insects and small invertebrates across the forest floor.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eublepharis hardwickii* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eublepharis hardwickii* is found in eastern and central India, specifically across Odisha, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, at low to moderate elevations.
